Population Statistics for Connecticut
Prepared by Karyn Backus and Lloyd Mueller
CT Department of Public Health
Annual Estimates
The populations of Connecticut at the state, county and town level are estimated at the calendar year midpoint (July 1) each year and are known as annual or mid-year estimates. The annual estimates are the  official  estimates for Connecticut and are the basis for calculating annual population rates. Annual estimates are also known as post-censal estimates because the USCB uses a variety of population change factors (births, deaths, Federal tax returns, Medicare enrollment, and immigration) to update the decennial census base counts from April 1, 2010. Although the April 1, 2010 census is an actual count of the population on that day, a mid-year estimate (July 1) better represents the population count for an entire year. Thus, annual (post-censal) estimates are created to serve as the best representation of a single year’s population and to provide a consistent reference point across years.
→ Annual Population Counts only:
Total Population for CT: State, County, Town as of July 1
The USCB’s post-censal estimates are published about a year following the estimate date (e.g., July 1, 2008 data will be published around July 1, 2009). Once the USCB releases the annual estimate, our DPH reviews the USCB’s annual estimates and makes any necessary adjustments. Our DPH then releases the official population estimates for Connecticut at the state, county, and town levels by October of the year following the estimate date. Included with each release of data is a discussion of the methodology used to calculate the estimates with special attention to changes in the USCB methodology and to any DPH adjustments.
• Annual town population data contains estimates annually as of July 1 by county/town.
• The USCB does not publish annual demographic data at the town-level.
